Triage: `domain:identity` (fix lands in `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts`), `pm:blocked` on the card's own `Blocked-by: #8049` line — the suggested fix (delete the inline copy, call `resolveActor`) is only correct once PR #8101 lands, so this waits for that merge and the unlock scan returns it. Type: Bug (declared control — the D5.1 env-access gate — silently unenforced for the documented API-lane credential spelling).

Grading note for the unlock re-check: severity is honestly bounded by the card itself (gate only configured on the cloud control plane; cookie path — which normalizes — is the common one; no live bearer-driven `/oauth2/authorize` measured). At requeue time re-verify on the merged ref that (a) #8101 didn't already absorb this site, and (b) the inline copy still exists at ~`:1341-1362`. The regression pin the card names (signed bearer + deny-configured gate ⇒ refused, not fall-through) should be a dispatch requirement — this is exactly the enforced-for-one-spelling class where a green suite proves the wrong thing.

## Both of triage's re-check conditions, run on the merged ref

The grading note asked for two readings at requeue time. Neither was assumed:

| triage's condition | reading on `origin/main` |
|:--|:--|
| (a) did #8101 already absorb this site? | **No.** `resolveActor(ctx)` at `:1302` serves the `/sso/register` branch; the `/oauth2/authorize` branch is separate |
| (b) does the inline copy still exist? | **Yes** — `gateUserId` with its own lookup at `:1329-1364` (the card said ~`:1341-1362`; drifted, as everything in this file has today) |

And the divergence the card predicted is now real and visible: `resolveActor` gained its signature-stripping fix at `:3832` (`const unsigned = …`), while the inline copy did not. Two resolution sites, one fixed, one not — exactly the shape that produced this card.

## Why this ranks now rather than later, despite honest severity bounds

The card bounds its own severity carefully — `oidcAuthorizeGate` is set only on the cloud control plane, the authorize endpoint is normally cookie-driven, and no live bearer-driven request was measured. I am not inflating that.

**But the failure mode is the worst-shaped one available**: the unresolved case is deliberately **fail-open** (*"Unauthenticated → fall through so the OP redirects to login"*), so an *authenticated* caller holding the documented API-lane credential is treated as unauthenticated and the env-access check **never evaluates**. A control that is enforced for one credential spelling and silently absent for the other, with zero test coverage (`oidcAuthorizeGate` appears in no `*.test.ts`) — that is #8049's lesson one endpoint over, and #8049 is the card that proved the shape is real rather than theoretical.
